# Track Distance Fix

> GPX distance correction for track runs. This local-first web tool estimates completed track laps and partial progress, then calculates selected-lane distance from a GPX file.

## Product Contract
- The runner uploads a GPX file and explicitly selects lane 1-8.
- GPX parsing and analysis happen in the browser. Coordinates, timestamps, and analysis results are not sent to an application backend.
- Loading the hosted web page still downloads its bundled HTML, JavaScript, CSS, fonts, and images from the host.
- Corrected distance is always `estimated total_laps * selected_lane_length`.
- Raw GPX distance is diagnostic only.
- Completed laps and an explicitly estimated angular final partial lap are shown separately.
- Intentional direction changes after completed laps are supported; traveled progress in both directions is added instead of cancelling out.
- Completed-lap time and pace are available when timestamps permit. The pace chart contains unconnected completed-lap observations and the table remains their exact-value source.
- Eligible completed laps may also show two unconnected estimated half-lap pace points. Half-lap values have no exact table, value-bearing tooltip, or fastest-half ranking; a half is half the selected lane length, not always 200 m.

## Evidence and Limits
- In controlled synthetic 10-lap traces, clean lane-1 and lane-6 cases had effectively zero lap-count and distance error.
- A controlled lane-8 trace with deterministic 3 m coordinate noise had 0.00928-lap error, equivalent to 4.202 m.
- A noisy controlled 6 + 4 direction-reversal trace was recovered as approximately 10 laps.
- A separate noisy synthetic fixture recovered all 20 reference half-lap boundaries inside the 10 m gate. It is not independent real-world validation.
- These deterministic fixtures are bounded evidence, not a universal guarantee for every device or recording.
- Three real lane-6 recordings from one runner are regression fixtures. Their lap totals and crossing times were verified manually, and the analysis results agree with them.
- Completed-lap topology is better supported than within-lap position. The final partial lap remains an angular estimate.
- The product deliberately omits exact 200 m, 100 m, and straight-only timing.
- Missing or invalid timestamps disable timing. Long gaps, noise, sparse traces, partial laps, discontinuous segments, and a dominant dense off-track cluster can weaken interpretation.
- The 5 km markers use estimated within-lap position and have a known outer-lane limitation.

## Lane Lengths
- Lane 1: 400.000 m
- Lane 2: 407.038 m
- Lane 3: 414.704 m
- Lane 4: 422.370 m
- Lane 5: 430.034 m
- Lane 6: 437.700 m
- Lane 7: 445.366 m
- Lane 8: 453.032 m

The table follows the World Athletics measurement convention for a standard 400 m track. The selected lane remains authoritative.

## Delivery
- The Vite static web build and deployment to `https://piotrkacala.pl/400m/` remain supported.
